children.value: High Demand for CNAs in California

The Certified Nurse Assistant Program (CNAP) offers resources to help you navigate the structured paths to become a CNA. With CNAP you can create your CNA story with confidence, unlocking a world of opportunities, and paving your way to success in the healthcare industry.
Whether you choose the Earn and Learn path or follow the traditional self-funded path, CNAP provides support to training programs you need to start your career with confidence.

children.value: CHOOSE YOUR PATH
Path 1:  Earn and Learn

Take advantage of the California Department of Public Health (CDPH) approved Earn and Learn Programs that allow you to start your CNA journey with no prior experience. Through this pathway you can earn a wage while you learn, gaining practical experience and receiving valuable training from experienced professionals.

children.value: Timing

Both training paths require a minimum of 160 hours total – 60 hours of theory and 100 hours of clinical practice approved by the California Department of Public Health. 
Most CNA training programs can take between 6-12 weeks, depending on if the classes are full-time or part-time. 
Many programs provide flexible options for people who are working or have other obligations.

children.value: Download the CNA Upskilling Timeline
Already certified?
If you’re already a CNA, don’t miss out on the opportunities that await you. Employers understand the value of investing in their workforce, including experienced CNAs like you.

Through the CNA Upskilling Program (CUSP), you’ll have the chance to advance through recognized levels of achievement based on your completed educational modules and work experience. As you progress, you’ll not only gain new certifications and skills, but also enjoy the financial rewards that come with each level of accomplishment.
CUSP offers a pathway for your continued growth and professional advancement.
